transcript:
Header: Northstar Financial 
Date: 2026-12-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~40 minutes
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Alicia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Mitchell (Head of Cloud Ops), Daniel Reyes (CISO), Priya Singh (Compliance), Ethan Brooks (Platform)

Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Northstar evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for financial workloads; main concerns are GDPR/data residency, PCI/HIPAA overlap, logging restrictions and auditability.
- Key ask: can we guarantee EU-only data residency, disable retention of raw transcripts, and support BYOK/KMS + HSM?
- Next: send security pack, schedule SE deep dive on network and key management, price Dedicated and Private options.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alicia from redwood, and i'll pass to marcus to do a quick architecture run-through and then we can jump into your questions around residency and compliance.
[00:12] Marcus Patel: yeah hi all, marcus here, se. quick agenda — how our hosted, dedicated, private options look, controls we provide for logs/retention, kms/byok — sorry byok — and then q and a.
[00:23] Laura Mitchell: great thanks. to set the context, northstar is evaluating chat + ingestion pipelines for customer support and fraud signals. security and residency are showstoppers for us. we need all eu customer data to stay in eu, and for certain flows we need on-prem or customer-managed keys.
[00:38] Daniel Reyes: and from a ciso perspective, we need SOC2, evidence of encryption at rest and transit, and the ability to limit any logging that could contain pii. also curious about hipaa implications even though we are financial, sometimes we handle health-adjacent data.
[00:52] Marcus Patel: makes sense. high-level: our hosted api runs in multiple regions, you can pin workloads to eu-west-1 and we support region-restricted routing. hosted has the fastest onboarding. Dedicated gives you reserved gpu pools per tenant with network isolation and more controls over logging and batch retention. Private is fully customer-managed — vpc, private control plane, can be on-prem.
[01:15] Priya Singh: ok on the hosted option — can we opt out of any analytics collection? we can't have raw transcripts retained by the vendor for more than 30 days, and ideally zero retention of raw audio/utf8 transcripts.
[01:27] Marcus Patel: yes, we have configurations. for hosted you can choose minimal retention where logs are ephemeral; we also offer a no-logging mode for certain invoiced enterprise tiers where we disable telemetry that contains user input. i will caveat that full-zero-retention on hosted is subject to contract and audit — for true policy enforcement we usually recommend Dedicated or Private.
[01:47] Laura Mitchell: what's the difference between dedicated and private when it comes to key management?
[01:52] Marcus Patel: Dedicated: we can do bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with cloud KMS integrations — you retain control of the master key in your cloud provider, but our runtime can call the key for model artifacts and token encryption. Private: you get full control, you can run our control plane behind your network and integrate with your on-prem hsm, or use a customer-managed hsm. so private is the highest assurance if you need HSM-backed keys and no vendor access.
[02:19] Ethan Brooks: regarding data flows — do you ever send logs back to us or third parties? any telemetry sent to redwood central?
[02:26] Marcus Patel: by default operational telemetry (metrics and service health) goes to our monitoring, but customer data and prompt content do not leave the assigned region for Dedicated/Private if configured. For hosted we isolate by region but some operational logs may hybridize — we can provide a control plane that has geo-residency controls, but the strictest guarantee is Private.
[02:46] Daniel Reyes: we need audit logs that show access to keys and to model inference. do you provide immutable audit trails?
[02:52] Marcus Patel: yes, we provide audit logs for API calls, key usage events, and admin actions. logs can be exported to your SIEM (splunk, sumo logic, datadog) or to an s3 compatible bucket in your account for retention. we also support write-once retention policies for audit buckets.
[03:06] Priya Singh: about gdpr — can you demonstrate data subject access request workflows? how do you delete a subject's data from embeddings or logs?
[03:14] Marcus Patel: good question. we support deletion endpoints and can run targeted redaction on stored artifacts. embeddings are considered derived data; we can identify and delete vectors associated with a subject id if you have an index mapping. for hosted we recommend tightly controlled TTLs. for private, this is under your control entirely.
[03:34] Laura Mitchell: our legal team also asked about cross-border transfer risk — we need to avoid any jurisdiction where u.s. law could compel vendor access. is private the only option to insulate that?
[03:44] Alicia Chen: i'll jump in — private is the strongest mitigation because you're running the control plane and keys in your jurisdiction. dedicated helps but there is still an operational contract; we do offer contractual commitments and data processing addenda aligned to gdpr for dedicated and hosted eu-only instances.
[04:00] Marcus Patel: also worth noting we offer contractual SLOs and contractual clauses that state data will be processed only in the designated region; but legal still has to weigh whether the vendor's home jurisdiction presents risk.
[04:12] Daniel Reyes: on logging restrictions — some of our compliance leads want zero retention for prompts that include pii, but keep non-sensitive metrics. can you support field-level redaction or token-level hashing before writing logs?
[04:23] Marcus Patel: yes, we have a redaction pipeline you can enable to scrub PII. patterns can be regex-based or rule-based, and you can also do client-side redaction before sending. additionally, we support hashing or tokenization of certain fields and you can route scrubbed logs to your audit bucket.
[04:40] Priya Singh: hipaa — we don't handle ePHI primarily, but there are cases. is redwood willing to sign a business associate agreement (BAA) or provide hipaa controls?
[04:50] Alicia Chen: we have customers in healthcare and financial services. we can discuss BAA — that's typical for private deployments or dedicated with contractual commitments. we will share our HIPAA control mappings in the security pack.
[05:03] Laura Mitchell: what's your SOC 2 status? and do you have iso 27001?
[05:08] Marcus Patel: we are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO certifications for the hosted control plane. i'll include the latest audit reports in the packet.
[05:15] Ethan Brooks: operationally — network peering and VPC setup: for dedicated, can you peer into our account or do you require an ingress? we want minimal exposure.
[05:26] Marcus Patel: we support multiple deployment modes: VPC peering into your account, VPC endpoint services, or private link equivalents depending on cloud provider. for Dedicated we typically peer and place instances in a dedicated subnet; for Private we can install into your k8s/on-prem cluster.
[05:41] Daniel Reyes: what about logging retention windows? regulatory sometimes wants 7 years. do you store forever or can we configure per-log type retention?
[05:50] Marcus Patel: retention is fully configurable. audit logs you can push to your S3 with lifecycle rules for 7 years. operational debug logs are configurable with short TTLs. we also support automatic purge of prompts after X days based on policy.
[06:05] Laura Mitchell: any limits on disabling model telemetry? like model usage stats or basic ops? we need monitoring but not content telemetry.
[06:13] Marcus Patel: yes you can disable content telemetry while keeping metrics like token counts, latency, error rates. content-level traces are disabled in the no-content-telemetry mode.
[06:24] Priya Singh: curious about embedding storage — if we delete a customer, how do you purge embeddings from vector dbs that may be shared?
[06:32] Marcus Patel: embeddings tied to a namespace or collection can be deleted; we recommend per-customer namespaces. shared indexes are an anti-pattern for regulated workloads.
[06:43] Ethan Brooks: on the private option — what are typical infra requirements and patch cadence? our infra team is worried about keeping runtime up to date.
[06:52] Marcus Patel: private comes as a package with an ops guide: k8s 1.25+ preferred, helm charts, docker images, and we provide monthly patch manifests. we can offer managed patching as an add-on where Redwood ops will push security updates during approved maintenance windows.
[07:08] Alicia Chen: let's talk about latency/cost tradeoffs quickly — dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower per-token cost for steady state. hosted is variable cost but fastest to start. private is the most control but higher operational overhead.
[07:22] Laura Mitchell: for a pilot, could we start hosted in eu and then move to dedicated if all good? what does migration look like?
[07:29] Marcus Patel: yes, you can start hosted and then migrate; we support model pinning and export of prompt logs and embeddings. we can help with a migration plan — typically a 2-4 week effort depending on volume.
[07:41] Daniel Reyes: are there any parts of the hosted deployment that permanently store customer inputs for model fine-tuning or improvement?
[07:49] Marcus Patel: not by default. we do not use customer prompts for improving public models unless you opt into a data sharing program. Enterprise customers can disable any training data retention.
[07:59] Priya Singh: ok would like to see concrete configs. can you show example policy YML for log retention and redaction?
[08:06] Marcus Patel: yes, i'll include sample policy snippets in the pack — examples for S3 lifecycle, redaction regex, and SIEM mapping.
[08:16] Ethan Brooks: one more technical nuance — how do you handle cryptographic key rotation with BYOK? we need key rotation without downtime.
[08:24] Marcus Patel: our KMS integrations support key rotation; we do seamless rotation by referencing key aliases and doing rolling re-encryption. for HSM on private, rotation is handled by your ops and we support zero-downtime key roll patterns with staged rewrap.
[08:38] Laura Mitchell: what's the process for an audit — can we get access to auditor read-only views or do we provide exported evidence?
[08:45] Marcus Patel: auditors can be granted read-only access under NDA for Dedicated/Private, or we provide exported artifacts and the SOC 2 report. we also offer a collab model where we meet with your auditors.
[08:58] Daniel Reyes: any specific controls around accidental data exfiltration — alerts, DLP hooks?
[09:04] Marcus Patel: yes we support DLP hooks and can integrate with your event pipeline. you can set rules to block or redacted content pre-ingest; alerts can be pushed to your security team.
[09:15] Alicia Chen: sounds like a lot of alignment — maybe we pause and see if there are any blockers or gotchas we should call out.
[09:20] Priya Singh: one blocker is legal's position on vendor jurisdiction. they will likely require private or a contract with a specific data processing addendum. another is cost — private looks expensive.
[09:31] Laura Mitchell: timeline: we need a pilot in q1 if possible, procurement has a 6-8 week lead time.
[09:38] Alicia Chen: noted. for pilots usually hosted in eu with no-content-telemetry or a dedicated trial environment is fastest.
[09:46] Marcus Patel: i'll also prepare an architecture diagram for a dedicated deployment with vpc peering, kms in your account, and log export.
[09:56] Ethan Brooks: what about rate limits for dedicated pilots — can we get throughput guarantees?
[10:02] Marcus Patel: Dedicated comes with reserved capacity; we will size based on your expected RPS and token rates. for pilots we typically provision a smaller pool and monitor.
[10:12] Daniel Reyes: ok good. last question — do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[10:17] Marcus Patel: yes, SAML, OIDC, SCIM, RBAC — full enterprise identity integrations.
[10:24] Laura Mitchell: anything else we should know about compliance packaging?
[10:28] Alicia Chen: we'll include a compliance matrix mapping to gdpr, hipaa, pci (your legal asked about pci earlier), and SOC 2 controls.
[10:36] Priya Singh: pci — we do have cardholder data in a few workflows; can you be pci compliant?
[10:42] Marcus Patel: we can support pci scoped deployments, usually by isolating cardholder data flows and redacting before it hits the model. private deployments are recommended for full pci scope.
[10:54] Laura Mitchell: okay let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[10:58] Alicia Chen: recap — redwood to send security pack (SOC2, iso, hipaa mapping, gdpr dpa), sample retention and redaction configs, dedicated/private pricing, and an architecture diagram for dedicated with VPC peering and BYOK. we'll also schedule an se deep dive for network and kms.
[11:16] Daniel Reyes: thanks. expect input from legal and platform on VPC topology and data classification. we'll aim to reconvene after you send docs.
[11:25] Marcus Patel: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive and upload artifacts to the shared folder.
[11:33] Laura Mitchell: thanks alicia and marcus, talk soon.

(Transcript ends — timestamps approximate; transcription contains minor errors and speaker attribution may be imperfect.)
